# Specification Quality Checklist: CodeRabbit Configuration Optimization

**Purpose**: Validate the quality, clarity, and completeness of requirements in the CodeRabbit configuration optimization feature specification.

**Created**: 2026-09-11

**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) — Complete feature specification with 5 user stories (P1-P3), 15 functional requirements, 13 measurable success criteria

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command as a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.

**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a requirements-quality validation tool. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.

**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality (the requirement is well-written, clear, testable, and complete). It does NOT mean implementation work is complete.

- [ ] CHK007 — Are requirements documented for all 30+ branch types with context-aware review guidance (FR-006, FR-013)? [Completeness, Spec §Branch Strategy]

## Requirement Clarity (Are requirements specific, unambiguous, and quantified?)

- [ ] CHK013 — Is "95%+ file type coverage" (SC-001) quantified with: baseline (80%), measurement method, and acceptance threshold? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK014 — Are "3+ specific review focus areas" (SC-002) defined with examples of what constitutes a "focus area"? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK015 — Is "85% of reviews cite specific guidance" (SC-009) measurable with: audit method, sample size, and pass criteria? [Clarity, Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK016 — Are vague terms like "comprehensive", "prominent", "aligned" replaced with measurable criteria throughout? [Clarity, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK017 — Is "technology-agnostic" guidance (FR-006 constraint) defined with explicit examples of what IS and IS NOT allowed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, §Constraints]
- [ ] CHK018 — Are path pattern priority levels (90-100 exact, 70-89 specific, etc.) clearly defined with rule examples? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK019 — Is the "first-matching-pattern" resolution rule documented (no cascading, priority order enforced)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK020 — Are branch type context requirements documented for each major branch type (security/, perf/, a11y/, docs/, feat/, fix/)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK021 — Is the <5 minute target for adding new file type instructions (SC-010) quantified with: operation scope, complexity limits, and success criteria? [Clarity, Spec §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK022 — Are "top 15 branch types" (SC-011) explicitly listed by name rather than implied? [Clarity, Spec §SC-011]

## Technology-Agnosticism Validation (Do all instructions apply universally across WordPress, Node.js, infrastructure, MCP?)

- [ ] CHK031 — Are any CodeRabbit instructions WordPress-specific (e.g., "use hooks", "actions/filters")? [Constraint violation check, Gap]
- [ ] CHK032 — Are any instructions Node.js/TypeScript-specific (e.g., "use async/await", "npm packages")? [Constraint violation check, Gap]
- [ ] CHK033 — Are any instructions infrastructure/Terraform-specific (e.g., "module structure", "provider config")? [Constraint violation check, Gap]
- [ ] CHK034 — Are any instructions MCP/AI-specific (e.g., tool names, protocol details)? [Constraint violation check, Gap]
- [ ] CHK035 — Do path instruction examples avoid framework/language specifics and reference only universal principles (code quality, security, performance, accessibility)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006 constraint]
- [ ] CHK036 — Are cross-technology validation scenarios (Scenario 11 in quickstart) comprehensive enough to prove organisation-wide applicability? [Coverage, Spec §Quickstart §Scenario 11]
- [ ] CHK037 — Is "technology stack diversity" context (plan.md §Technology Stack Diversity) reflected in guidance requirements (no framework assumptions)? [Consistency, Spec vs Plan context]
- [ ] CHK038 — Do branch context requirements (security/, perf/, a11y/, etc.) avoid project-type assumptions (all guidance applies to WordPress, Node.js, infrastructure, MCPs equally)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Unresolved items should remain unchecked until clarified, corrected, or explicitly documented as intentional gaps
- This checklist focuses on requirements quality (well-written, complete, clear, testable, consistent) NOT implementation completeness
- Reference sections by full path when citing spec (e.g., [Spec §User Stories] means spec.md §User Stories)
- Use `[Gap]` marker when identifying missing requirements; use `[Ambiguity]` for unclear items; use `[Consistency]` for conflicts
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state and uses it as a validation gate; authors do not modify markers
